title: Business Central v29: Using AL Interfaces with Default Method Support
summary: Business Central 29.0 introduces default interface methods in AL, allowing interfaces to provide complete procedure implementations that codeunits may override while maintaining backward compatibility. This feature reduces duplicate code and lets developers evolve interfaces without breaking existing implementations.
key_points: Default interface methods let an interface carry a full procedure body that implementing codeunits either inherit or override
Abstract members hold only a signature and must be implemented; default members run automatically unless overridden
A default method can only be called through an interface variable, not directly on a codeunit that does not define it
To add a mandatory procedure safely, first add it with a default body, then mark it RequiredPending to warn implementors, then remove the body
The author notes that interfaces in general help AI code generation by giving a strict contract to follow

quotes.text: A default method lets the interface provide a full implementation that codeunits may override if needed.
quotes.why_it_matters: This is the core capability that solves the problem of adding functionality to interfaces without breaking existing implementations

quotes.text: To access default implementations, you must call the interface variable not the code unit directly.
quotes.why_it_matters: Understanding this distinction is critical for developers to correctly implement the feature; calling the wrong reference type will cause compilation errors

quotes.text: Default Interface Methods make interfaces far more flexible and reduce the risk of breaking existing implementations when requirements evolve.
quotes.why_it_matters: This summarizes the main business value of the feature for maintaining stable systems while evolving architecture
